account: Something unusual is being organized around this evening's eighteen-hundred appointment in the great hall. The innkeeper described a hospitality committee involving the innkeeper, builder and freight, said bread was reserved, and promised explanations at eighteen. I agreed not to arrive early. Freight checked that the hall would be available, and the secretary intends to escort me inside precisely then. Neighbour reported 201 fresh loaves in the hall, baked yesterday. That quantity and the insistence on timing suggest a substantial gathering, perhaps a surprise celebration or communal hospitality event, but I do not know its real purpose or guests. Townspeople repeatedly mention a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' One report associated baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour with it, and said builder carried a sack of bread from the bakery. These reports may relate to the gathering, but I have not verified what changed or witnessed it myself. I visited the bakery today but did not find the baker. Ordinary official business has been oddly thin: no council letters or account ledgers have been provided, and my ten-o'clock mill inspection had no apparent host or grain report. The secretary says the inspection was already on my schedule and does not know who arranged it. This could be mundane disorganization rather than concealment. I have kept my appointments and am now home after the scheduled noon lunch period, with the secretary outside. Next are council letters at thirteen, tea with neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and the hall meeting at eighteen. I should keep these commitments and seek firsthand explanations without treating rumours as established facts.
